text.arabic_uthmani: فَلَا تَعْجَلْ عَلَيْهِمْ ۖ إِنَّمَا نَعُدُّ لَهُمْ عَدًّۭا

words.gloss_range: consequential conjunction that carries the prior ayah into the prohibition clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the whole opening prohibition complex launched by the consequential particle

words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) makes the opening prohibition a consequence, not a detached command. It brings the agitation of 19:83 into the new ayah and launches the whole complex {{ar:فَلَا تَعْجَلْ عَلَيْهِمْ}} ({{tr:fa-la taʿjal ʿalayhim}}), so the reader hears the restraint as the commanded response to what has just been disclosed.

topics.headline: consequential prohibition link
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command not to hasten is the immediate consequence of the prior scene in 19:83, not a free-standing moral maxim.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) as a conjunction introducing a consequential clause, and attachment evidence makes words 1-4 the prohibitive verbal clause linked to the following explanation.

words.gloss_range: prohibitive negation governing a jussive verb, with scope limited to the first clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the jussive verb governed by the prohibitive particle
the affirmative restricted explanation that follows the prohibition

words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:la}}) is the prohibitive particle, so the clause commands non-hastening rather than reporting that haste does not occur. Its force stops at {{ar:تَعْجَلْ}} ({{tr:taʿjal}}); the later {{ar:إِنَّمَا نَعُدُّ}} ({{tr:innama naʿuddu}}) remains an affirmative restricted explanation for the command.

topics.headline: prohibitive jussive scope
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a direct restraint command whose negation governs only the haste clause while the counting clause stays positively asserted.
topics.reason: QAC identifies {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:la}}) as a jussive negation particle, and attachment evidence defines words 1-4 as the prohibitive clause with words 5-9 as its explanation.

words.gloss_range: prohibited haste or premature pressure, locally directed through {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿala}}) toward the plural group
words.root_gloss_range: haste, immediacy, premature action, and quick movement; local grammar selects restrained premature pressure, not unrelated root branches

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the prepositional target of the prohibited haste
the prohibitive particle that halts the haste verb

words.prose: {{ar:تَعْجَلْ}} ({{tr:taʿjal}}) is visibly jussive after the prohibition, and its second-person singular form keeps one addressee distinct from the plural target. The root makes the blocked act a premature push, while the following {{ar:عَلَيْهِمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhim}}) directs that impatience against them. The tight consonantal rush of {{ar:تَعْجَلْ}} ({{tr:taʿjal}}) is stopped by {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:la}}) before it reaches that adversarial phrase. The broader haste field is narrowed here: this is not a request that God hasten events, but the addressee's own urgency being halted. That local restraint also meets larger haste scenes, including prophetic restraint at 20:114 and 75:16 and the haste-counting contrast at 22:47.

topics.headline: visible direct restraint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the form itself issues a direct singular command, not a general statement about haste.
topics.reason: QAC tags the word as an imperfect jussive second-person masculine singular verb, and the prohibitive particle before it supplies the command force.

topics.headline: premature pressure root
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prohibited haste is premature timing-pressure rather than ordinary speed.
topics.reason: The root field supports haste before its proper time, but local grammar narrows the broader concrete and timing branches to prohibited premature pressure in the ayah.

topics.headline: against-them direction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the haste is not merely internal impatience; it is pointed through {{ar:عَلَيْهِمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhim}}) toward the same group.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:عَلَيْهِمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhim}}) a prepositional complement of the verb, so mixed transitivity claims survive only as outward pressure through {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿala}}), not as a direct-object construction.

topics.headline: haste-counting correction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the halted haste is answered by divine counting, with 22:47 providing a concrete cross-reference where hastening and counting meet.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete prophetic-restraint and haste-counting references, and no guardrail evidence contradicts using them as parallels rather than as controllers of the local parse.

topics.headline: halted sound boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the quick consonantal pressure of {{ar:تَعْجَلْ}} ({{tr:taʿjal}}) being stopped by the prohibition before it reaches the group.
topics.reason: The sound-texture rows are locally tied to the surface form and to the boundary from 19:83 into the prohibition, so they can remain as a secondary payoff.

words.gloss_range: preposition {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿala}}) with third-person plural suffix, marking the target of prohibited pressure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the prepositional base inside the local target phrase

words.prose: {{ar:عَلَيْهِمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhim}}) keeps the disbelieving group from 19:83 in view, but it makes them an oblique prepositional target rather than a direct object. The relation is pressure upon or against them; the obligation sense of {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿala}}) is not the local reading. This first preposition later contrasts with {{ar:لَهُمْ}} ({{tr:lahum}}): haste toward them is forbidden, while a tally is assigned to them.

topics.headline: continuing plural referent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the pronoun does not introduce a new target; it carries forward the group named in 19:83.
topics.reason: Attachment cross-reference evidence resolves the suffixes in {{ar:عَلَيْهِمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhim}}) and {{ar:لَهُمْ}} ({{tr:lahum}}) back to the disbelievers just mentioned.

topics.headline: oblique adversarial target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prohibited haste is directed against the group through a preposition, not imposed as a direct verbal object or duty toward them.
topics.reason: The attachment marks {{ar:عَلَيْهِمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhim}}) as the prepositional complement of {{ar:تَعْجَلْ}} ({{tr:taʿjal}}), narrowing broader {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿala}}) possibilities to adversarial direction here.

topics.headline: preposition contrast with {{tr:lahum}}
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a structural contrast: human pressure is blocked against them, while divine accounting is later marked for them.
topics.reason: Both prepositional phrases are syntactically attached to their verbs, allowing the CRITICAL contrast between {{ar:عَلَيْهِمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhim}}) and {{ar:لَهُمْ}} ({{tr:lahum}}) to survive.

words.gloss_range: restrictive particle opening the explanatory counting clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the emphatic particle element restrained in the fused restrictive form
the following counting verb restricted by the particle

words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّمَا}} ({{tr:innama}}) pivots from the prohibition into a restricted explanation. As a fused restrictive particle, it does not set up an ordinary governed noun after {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}); it lets {{ar:نَعُدُّ}} ({{tr:naʿuddu}}) stand as the restricted verbal assertion. The payoff is agency: the addressee must not force the timing because the divine speaker is already the one counting.

topics.headline: fused restrictive particle
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that {{ar:إِنَّمَا}} ({{tr:innama}}) creates restriction while leaving the following counting verb as a verbal clause.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the particle as {{tr:kaffa-makfufa}}, supporting the CRITICAL claim that the fused surface unit restricts rather than governing a following accusative noun.

topics.headline: exclusive divine counting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reason for restraint is not delay or neglect, but restricted divine agency already engaged in counting.
topics.reason: The second clause is explicitly linked as the explanation for the first, and {{ar:إِنَّمَا}} ({{tr:innama}}) scopes over {{ar:نَعُدُّ}} ({{tr:naʿuddu}}), so the agency-and-justification rows are locally licensed.

words.gloss_range: ongoing divine counting, with the counted item unexpressed and the account assigned by {{ar:لَهُمْ}} ({{tr:lahum}})
words.root_gloss_range: counting, enumerating, reckoning, preparing, and timed recurrence; local form selects active enumeration/reckoning in progress

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the restrictive particle governing the counting assertion
the dative account-holder phrase attached to the counting verb
the same-root cognate accusative that closes and intensifies the count
the prohibited haste verb answered by the counting assertion

words.prose: {{ar:نَعُدُّ}} ({{tr:naʿuddu}}) shifts the ayah from what the addressee must not do to what the divine speaker is already doing. The first-person plural imperfect makes the count ongoing and restricted by {{ar:إِنَّمَا}} ({{tr:innama}}), while the actual counted item remains unspoken. The verb therefore presents a live tally assigned to them through {{ar:لَهُمْ}} ({{tr:lahum}}), not a disclosed final number. Its doubled sound is picked up by the same-root closure {{ar:عَدًّا}} ({{tr:ʿadda}}), making the counting feel compact, repeated, and active. It answers {{ar:تَعْجَلْ}} ({{tr:taʿjal}}) within the ayah and also meets the haste-counting field at 22:47 and the same-surah counting return at 19:94.

topics.headline: restricted divine imperfect
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine counting is presented as an ongoing first-person act, contrasted with the addressee's jussive restraint.
topics.reason: QAC marks {{ar:نَعُدُّ}} ({{tr:naʿuddu}}) as a first-person plural imperfect indicative, and the preceding restrictive particle makes that implicit subject the restricted counting agent.

topics.headline: live tally with hidden object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah asserts the reality of counting while withholding what exactly is being counted.
topics.reason: The attachment frame marks no expressed counted object for the verb while the cognate accusative appears later, so transitivity claims must be narrowed to an absolute counting process intensified by {{ar:عَدًّا}} ({{tr:ʿadda}}).

topics.headline: account assigned to them
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the group is not the direct object but the account-holder to whom the tally is assigned.
topics.reason: {{ar:لَهُمْ}} ({{tr:lahum}}) is attached as a prepositional complement of {{ar:نَعُدُّ}} ({{tr:naʿuddu}}), so the benefactive/adverse tension survives as dative reference rather than a direct counted object.

topics.headline: haste-counting and surah accounting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees divine enumeration replacing human urgency, with concrete echoes at 22:47 and 19:94.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL inter-ayah rows provide concrete references and are compatible with the local root and clause structure when used as echoes rather than replacements for the local parse.

topics.headline: cognate and sound convergence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the doubled sound and same-root closure make the counting feel repeated and active.
topics.reason: The later verbal noun is confirmed as a same-root cognate accusative, so the verb's sound and root repetition can be kept as a local form payoff.

words.gloss_range: preposition forming {{ar:لَهُمْ}} ({{tr:lahum}}), marking the group as the referenced account-holder

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the complete dative phrase formed by the preposition and pronoun

words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) is the preposition that makes the tally theirs without making them the direct object counted. It forms {{ar:لَهُمْ}} ({{tr:lahum}}), placing the account-holder between the counting verb and the final cognate noun. The form can sound like for-them reference, but context makes the assigned account ominous rather than beneficial.

topics.headline: dative account-holder
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the group is indexed as the holder of the account before the final counting noun lands.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}) governed by {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) and the resulting phrase a complement of {{ar:نَعُدُّ}} ({{tr:naʿuddu}}).

topics.headline: prepositional relation shift
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from pressure against them to an account assigned to them, with the apparent for-them form carrying adverse force in context.
topics.reason: The contrast with {{ar:عَلَيْهِمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhim}}) is syntactically licensed, but the benefactive wording is narrowed by context to dative reference for an ominous tally.

words.gloss_range: third-person plural pronoun governed by {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}), continuing the known disbelieving group

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the complete dative phrase containing the pronoun

words.prose: {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}) supplies the same plural group inside {{ar:لَهُمْ}} ({{tr:lahum}}). It is not an independent subject; it is the prepositional complement that makes the count belong to a known referent carried over from 19:83. The repeated pronoun lets the ayah contrast two relations to the same group: pressure upon them is forbidden, but accounting for them proceeds.

topics.headline: persistent known referent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the counted party is not newly introduced; the pronoun carries the group from 19:83 into divine accounting.
topics.reason: The attachment cross-reference resolves the pronoun chain to the disbelievers just mentioned, supporting the continuity claim.

topics.headline: bound prepositional complement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the pronoun's role is created by its prepositional host, so the same group can be governed differently in the two clauses.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the word as a third-person plural pronoun and attachment evidence makes it the complement of {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}), not an independent subject.

words.gloss_range: indefinite verbal noun functioning as cognate accusative, intensifying the counting while withholding the counted contents
words.root_gloss_range: counting, number, reckoning, preparation, counted time, and recurrence; local form selects the counting process as a cognate verbal noun

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the same-root counting verb that governs the final cognate accusative

words.prose: {{ar:عَدًّا}} ({{tr:ʿadda}}) closes the ayah with the noun of counting. As an indefinite cognate accusative of {{ar:نَعُدُّ}} ({{tr:naʿuddu}}), it confirms and intensifies the act without revealing the counted contents or final total. The maṣdar form selects process rather than a finished number, while the same-root echo and doubled sound make the close feel like tallying in motion. The broader root can include prepared provision and counted time, but here those branches are narrowed to an active reckoning whose finitude is echoed by counted-days references such as 2:184 and 3:24 and by the return of counting in 19:94.

topics.headline: indefinite undisclosed count
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the count is real but its total remains undisclosed.
topics.reason: QAC and noun-instance evidence identify the word as an indefinite verbal noun, supporting the unspecified-count payoff.

topics.headline: cognate process intensifier
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final noun is not the hidden thing counted; it is the verb's own noun intensifying the act of enumeration.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence explicitly marks {{ar:عَدًّا}} ({{tr:ʿadda}}) as a same-root cognate accusative of {{ar:نَعُدُّ}} ({{tr:naʿuddu}}), narrowing wider root senses such as regarding or considering to actual enumeration here.

topics.headline: finite accounting root field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that broader counted-time and preparation associations add finitude and readiness to the account, while local grammar keeps enumeration as the selected sense.
topics.reason: V4 preserves broader {{ar:ع د د}} ({{tr:ʿ-d-d}}) branches, but the cognate-accusative grammar anchors the local word in counting while allowing finitude echoes at 2:184, 3:24, and 19:94.

topics.headline: closure-weighted count
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah lands on counting itself, after identifying the account-holder first.
topics.reason: The word is final and follows {{ar:لَهُمْ}} ({{tr:lahum}}), so the CRITICAL closure and delayed-intensification rows are supported by local order.

topics.headline: root echo and audible tally
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the repeated root and doubled consonant turn the final word into an audible tally.
topics.reason: The verb and final verbal noun share the same root, and the surface form supports the sound-texture rows as local secondary payoff.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: تَعْجَلْ at word 2 is opposed to نَعُدُّ...عَدًّا at words 5 and 7.
baseline_models.mechanism: The prohibition blocks advancing an outcome before its time, while إِنَّمَا redirects agency from the addressee's haste to a presently operating exact enumeration.

activation_trace.role: Its speeding and advancing-before-time image supplies the human tempo being blocked.
Its exact-enumeration image supplies the measured process that replaces haste.

changed_reading.before: Do not hurry what will happen to them.
changed_reading.after: Do not advance their outcome yourself: an exact process is already running for them, so delay is active rather than empty.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The prohibition of premature speed and the cognate نَعُدُّ...عَدًّا construction jointly foreground timing.
baseline_models.mechanism: The counted-duration and scheduled-time branches let the count sound like a finite allotted interval being run to completion, not only objects being tallied.

activation_trace.role: Its before-the-appointed-time image creates the need for a term that must not be preempted.
Its counted-duration image turns enumeration into an allotted waiting period.
Its fixed-time image gives that period a scheduled endpoint.

changed_reading.before: We are tallying their deeds or persons.
changed_reading.after: We are counting out their allotted interval to completion; the ban on haste preserves that measured term.

context_deltas.mechanism: Writing fixes each utterance into an enforceable record while extension lengthens the punitive term; the focus count consequently becomes an accruing account with a temporal runway.

activation_trace.role: Enumeration supplies the account into which the earlier recorded material can accrue.
Its fixing that entails judgment turns what is said into an enforceable entry feeding the count.
Its lengthened-term image supplies the span across which the account continues to accrue.

structural_cues: 19:79 and 19:84 pair first-person-plural imperfect verbs with cognate accusatives: نَمُدُّ...مَدًّا and نَعُدُّ...عَدًّا.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies fixed writing, an extended term, and the matched construction; I infer that entries accrue through that extension into the focus count. A live alternative is rhetorical parallel with counting independent of writing.

changed_reading.before: The count is a bare tally or countdown.
changed_reading.after: The count is a continuously accruing, judgment-bearing record, making immediate intervention unnecessary.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding intensive agitation establishes a pressured rhythm; the focus prohibition refuses that rhythm and replaces it with measured enumeration.

activation_trace.role: Its premature-speed image identifies the reactive tempo the addressee must not adopt.
Its discrete enumeration supplies a controlled counter-rhythm.
Its boiling, sounding agitation image supplies the accelerated pressure immediately before the focus.

structural_cues: The adjacent intensive pair تُؤُزُّهُمْ أَزًّا is answered by فَلَا تَعْجَلْ عَلَيْهِمْ and the measured pair نَعُدُّ...عَدًّا.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacent agitation, prohibited haste, and count; I infer a warning against mirroring the tempo acting on them. The alternative is that the adjacency only intensifies their condition and says nothing about mimetic response.

changed_reading.before: Do not seek their outcome too soon.
changed_reading.after: Do not let their induced agitation set your pace; the divine count contains that acceleration within a different rhythm.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus count can function as a pre-dispatch muster: an enumerated population is assembled and then moved through sharply different procedures toward distinct destinations.

activation_trace.role: Its preparation image lets counting function as operational readiness for the movements that follow.
Its gathering and conducting a group to a destination turns readiness into assembly.
Its arrival before a sovereign marks the first assembled group's mode of reception.
Its driving and expulsion image supplies the contrasting transport imposed on the second group.
Its arrival-at-a-destination image completes the second dispatch lane.

structural_cues: The balanced adjacent clauses contrast نَحْشُرُ...وَفْدًا with نَسُوقُ...وِرْدًا immediately after the focus count.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies preparation, assembly, driving, and two arrival modes; I infer that enumeration serves as the manifest for ordered dispatch. The live alternative is simple chronological sequence without a logistical function for the count.

changed_reading.after: God is mustering them by count for a controlled sorting and dispatch, so the apparent wait is operational preparation.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later reprise joins exhaustive encompassment to the same count and then resolves the collective كُلُّهُمْ into فَرْدًا; the earlier لَهُمْ therefore denotes separately indexed persons rather than an undifferentiated mass.

activation_trace.role: The focus enumeration establishes the count whose unit is clarified later.
Its exhaustive-enumeration image removes the possibility of an approximate or merely collective count.
The exact lexical reprise carries the focus count into the later statement of total coverage.
Its solitary-unit image identifies each person as an irreducible item within the total.

structural_cues: 19:94 repeats عَدَّهُمْ عَدًّا, and 19:95 immediately pairs كُلُّهُمْ with فَرْدًا.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies exact lexical reprise, exhaustive coverage, and solitary arrival; I infer that persons are individually indexed in the earlier count. A live alternative is that 19:84 primarily counts days, deeds, or utterances while 19:94 counts persons.

changed_reading.before: We count them as a collective object of judgment.
changed_reading.after: Every member of the collective is already exhaustively and individually indexed; none is hidden inside the plural.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The count-to-zero model is surprising because no branch states numerical subtraction; it remains anchored in the focus enumeration and the later sequence of destruction, failed sensing, exhaustive negation, and inaudible trace. Render it only as a cross-domain metaphor for no detectable remainder, not as the ayah's asserted arithmetic.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: نَعُدُّ لَهُمْ عَدًّا can be carried forward as a process whose counted population eventually leaves no sensibly recoverable remainder.

activation_trace.role: Exact enumeration supplies the numerical frame from which the zero-remainder metaphor is inferred.
Its falling into destruction supplies the removal process.
Its sensory-detection image supplies the first test for any remainder.
Its exhaustive-negation image reduces the detectable persons to none.
Its faint-sound image supplies the final minimal trace that is no longer heard.

changed_reading.before: The count delays a future judgment.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the measured process runs a generation down to no detectable human or acoustic remainder.

strongest_changes: 19:83 turns the prohibition into a refusal to mirror the adversaries' agitated tempo.
19:94-95 resolves the count as exhaustive person-by-person indexing.
19:79 and 19:85-86 make the count active as both an accruing record and a pre-dispatch muster.
summary.what_was_special: The focus's haste/count opposition became a control-of-tempo mechanism: pressure accelerates, while inscription, enumeration, preparation, and individual dispatch proceed at a measured pace.
remaining_uncertainties: The counted unit may be persons, utterances, deeds, days, or several of these at once.
The preparation branch of ع د د may supply a genuine lexical activation or only a functional inference from the following muster.
The counter-rhythm reading depends on treating the adjacency and paired cognate constructions as mechanistically significant.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyi tek tek sayıp miktarını belirleme çekirdeğini; sayı, sayılan şey, sayıca çokluk ve bir topluluk içinde sayılma kullanımlarıyla birlikte açıkça destekler. branch_policy.note: No branch filtering is applied. Every branch present in each included dictionary/gloss root entry is kept.

root_mapping.policy: Use the dominant Furuq root for every QAC root, and include non-dominant Furuq targets as additional root_lexicon entries when qac-furuq-v4-root-map marks the QAC root as split.

root_lexicon.note: Turkish is the only language with dictionary entries/glosses currently sourced.
